item.title: MapQuest was gone for 20 fucking years and came back to fight the surveillance state. What a fucking timeline.
item.description:
Well, holy fucking shit. MapQuest is showing drivers where Flock surveillance cameras are located. The same technology that once helped us find the nearest gas station is now helping us see where Big Brother is watching. Apparently, knowing who's spying on you is fucking radical.
Here's the beautiful hypocrisy: the government and its corporate partners can photograph your license plate, record your movements, and build searchable databases of where you've been. But citizens mapping the cameras? Suddenly, transparency becomes a fucking problem. They'll sell you mass surveillance as "public safety" while quietly normalizing a society where everyone is tracked and nobody in power has to explain a goddamn thing. Funny how privacy becomes suspicious the moment ordinary people demand some for themselves. The people watching us shouldn't be the only ones who know where the cameras are. Surveillance without accountability isn't freedom. It's control with a fucking marketing department. Good on MapQuest. #PrivacyMatters #SurveillanceState #FlockSafety #BigBrother #CivilLiberties #MapQuest https://carbuzz.com/mapquest-showing-flock-camera-locations-october-2026/ https://imgur.com/gallery/8scigm9/comment/2515556119

item.title: GovBrief Today #628
item.description: Alina Habba was Donald Trump’s top federal prosecutor in New Jersey when a billionaire’s family guaranteed her a job paying more than $50 million. Julio Herrera Velutini had pleaded his bribery charges down to a misdemeanor, and he wanted even that gone. His daughter donated $3.5 million to a Trump super PAC. A lawyer from Trump’s personal legal team pushed for clemency, and the pardon still didn’t come. Then the family gave Habba the job. She started on January 1, and weeks later Trump fully pardoned him. She won’t say what she does for the company, which has no public profile. Habba says the Justice Department vetted the job. That’s the department that charged Herrera with bribing Puerto Rico’s governor. I’ve emailed 9,597 stories over 628 straight nights, free and without ads. The algorithm can’t show them all to you.
